source_quality.notes: text layer covers all 21 pages; the six displayed formulas were checked on the raster

task_reconstruction: Grade a city's smart growth by folding ten principles into five metrics, sum them to an index out of 100, score Sacramento and Edinburgh, and rescore both after new initiatives.

section_map.summary: the objective, the two cities and the scores
the ten principles and the objective

contributions.summary: an index that sums five metrics to a score out of 100
normalization against a named regional maximum
benchmarks of 44.7 and 54.9 for two cities
a rescoring that puts the gain at about ten points

dependency_graph.relation: the grouping is what the metrics measure

assumptions.summary: higher density means more people in vertical buildings
a higher ownership share means a wider range of housing
country transparency stands for the developers in one city
use of transit shows success better than what is offered

data_and_preprocessing.summary: density normalized by Los Angeles and Glasgow, park area by Honolulu
city budgets read by hand and sorted into restoration or new build
transparency taken from a country index
commute shares taken from census tables for ages 16 and up

models.summary: the index as an unweighted sum
land use as two normalized ratios averaged
community as crime and budget share averaged
development as four terms averaged, poverty flipped
transport as transit share plus walking share

verification.summary: two metrics checked against Los Angeles and New York
every measure moved by 10 and 20 percent
the initiatives rescored through the same index

results_trace.summary: Sacramento's transport score of 1.4, the lowest

writing_logic.summary: the summary states the objective before the method
each crude measure is conceded in the same paragraph that uses it
the allowed use is fenced before the results
the ranking is closed by saying it will not hold

language_observations.summary: opens on the objective rather than the background
concedes a measure is simple for a complex issue
names gentrification and then sets it outside the report
calls the weakness the trade the model was designed to make

visualization_observations.summary: a diagram reduces ten principles to five metrics to one index
a radar chart compares the five scores for both cities
the same chart redrawn before and after the initiatives
a matrix shows which principles share a core idea

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: admitting a measure is crude before using it reads as honest
claiming the weakness as an intended trade reads as self-aware

weaknesses.summary: the park normalizer is a median in the prose and a maximum in the formula
three measures are promised and four are used
dividing by two puts housing and transport on a smaller scale than the rest
only two metrics were tested and one term was dropped for the test

independent_extensions.summary: score a city measure as a ratio to the best case in its own region
test a plan by changing the inputs and running the same index again

unresolved_questions: the park normalizer is described as both a median and a maximum
no check is given that the five metrics actually share a 0 to 20 range
the new inputs after the initiatives are estimated rather than derived
the link between the metrics is named and then left unmodeled
the fifty percent population case is discussed without a table of its own
